claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
Adding a minor alloying element can improve the room-temperature compressive strength–plasticity balance of equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo.
Boron is proposed as the minor alloying addition.
The proposed effect is expected at room temperature when the minor-element content is below 1 at.%.
The minor alloying addition will refine the grain structure.
The minor alloying addition will reduce Mo segregation.
The minor alloying addition will promote a more homogeneous distribution of elements.
Grain refinement, reduced Mo segregation, and greater elemental homogeneity will improve plasticity without sacrificing strength.
The intervention will increase room-temperature compressive plasticity by at least 10% relative to the equiatomic disordered-BCC alloy.
The intervention will cause less than a 5% loss in strength relative to the equiatomic disordered-BCC alloy.
The baseline room-temperature compressive yield strength of equiatomic disordered-BCC NbZrTiHfMo is 1719 MPa.
Minor-element contents above 1 at.% may adversely affect strength and plasticity.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says strength will not be sacrificed, whereas the predicted outcome permits a strength loss of up to nearly 5%.
